A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same knowledge-manipulation study. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, references, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data retrieval, classification, comparison, and inverse-search experiments, plus GPT-3.5/4 evaluations, in Figures 3–7 and Appendices B–E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Llama/Mistral results, larger-scale experiments, and contemporary model examples, particularly in Figures 9–14.

M1.justification: The core BIO pretraining, LoRA QA finetuning, mixed training, and hint-based procedures are retained. Llama/Mistral are additional experimental subjects. The numbered-document mitigation elaborates the Bible retrieval procedure already described in v1 Appendix E.1.

E1.justification: The same biography, WikiBio, literary, and Chinese-language task coverage is retained. Larger bioS datasets use the same underlying attribute distribution and tasks. Birth-day comparisons and the Bible example already appeared in v1 Appendices C and E.1; their prominence in v2 does not establish new coverage.

E2.justification: v1's controlled experiments evaluate GPT2 architectures; v2 adds evaluated Llama and Mistral comparisons across retrieval, manipulation, and inverse-search experiments (Figures 10, 12–14). Figure 9 also adds Llama-3 alongside contemporary GPT-4 examples.

E3.justification: Added experiments expand bioS from 100,000 individuals to 1, 2, and 5 million, use full multi-infinity augmentation, introduce 2x/5.5x model configurations and native Llama/Mistral tokenizers, and extend manipulation training sets to 2.5 million individuals. Appendix C specifies a different learning rate for the larger Mistral experiment. These are additional settings, not replacements of the original GPT2 protocols.

E4.justification: Figures 10 and 12–14 substantially extend robustness analysis across architectures, model sizes, data sizes, and augmentation strength. v2 also reports answer-format/padding and beam-decoding checks and adds GPT-4/Llama-3 failure cases. The underlying Bible analysis was already present in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version provides seed-based uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both describe selecting the better result from alternative LoRA ranks and mixing ratios. Repeating experiments with different architectures in v2 does not introduce statistical replication reporting.

E6.justification: Original benchmark results are retained, including v1 Figure 9 as v2 Figure 11, while substantial numerical results are added in Figures 10(b–d) and 12–14. For example, Figure 13's hint-trained, BIO-initialized Mistral reports 78.9% major-subtraction accuracy with hints versus 1.2% without hints at 2.5 million training individuals. These are new-setting results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The LoRA formulation, sample-complexity arguments, and calculations relating hint accuracy to task accuracy are retained. The numbered Results 1–9 organize empirical findings and recommendations; they do not introduce new mathematical theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about difficult knowledge manipulation without CoT and failed inverse search remain. v2 adds a human-versus-LLM 'Turing test' contribution and elevates document rewriting and line numbering into explicit mitigation recommendations in Section 1.2, Result 9, and the conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations distinguishing stored-knowledge manipulation from in-context computation and relating partial-retrieval differences to tokenization. Section 5 changes BERT from a possible partial mitigation to an ineffective alternative because of its extraction difficulties. These refine interpretation while retaining the main autoregressive explanation.

D1.justification: Appendices B–D newly disclose deterministic beam-4 decoding and V100/A100 hardware, and specify added models' dimensions, native tokenizers, grouped-query attention, and the larger Mistral learning rate. The title-page footnote adds project and video links. Newly disclosed decoding details do not establish a change to the original experiments.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 substantially expands positioning relative to CoT and StrategyQA, distinguishes in-context reasoning from stored-knowledge manipulation, and connects the findings to reversal training and multi-token prediction. New references also cover Mistral, hidden computation, and related knowledge-capacity research.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, a separate contributions subsection is added, and findings throughout Sections 3–5 are reorganized into nine explicitly numbered results. Explanations, terminology, captions, and the conclusion receive substantial editing beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Bible illustration and contemporary-model examples, expands the old bioR retrieval figure into Figure 10's four panels, and adds Figures 12–14. Figure 4 is shortened while its omitted rows remain in the appendix, and Figure 6 is reformatted with explanatory text alongside it.

improvement.justification: v1 extrapolated broad conclusions from controlled GPT2 experiments; v2 adds controlled Llama/Mistral comparisons and much larger data and training sets, substantially strengthening the empirical foundation. Clearer result organization and additional implementation details also improve assessability. A material caveat remains: Section 4 calls major ranking barely above chance at 2.5 million examples, whereas Figure 13 reports 69.7–73.0% against a 50.5% baseline. This overstatement limits the conclusions, but the broader controlled evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
